newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 20.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
CASTE TO SHAPE PRIME MINISTER'S AGENDA FOR BUDGET

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda indicated the next budget would have many concessions for the backward classes. He said these concessions would help to rectify injustices committed against the weaker sections, at least to a certain extent. The prime minister also promised to set up a cabinet sub-committee to oversee the implementation of 27 percent reservations for Other Backward Castes (OBCs) in government jobs. Sources said these measures indicated the prime minister was keen to unfurl a caste-based political agenda.
The Hindustan Times
RAJASTHAN ASSEMBLY SESSION BEGINS TODAY

The winter session of the Rajasthan Assembly would begin on Monday amidst claims of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) rebels to bring down the state government if their demand for a change of leadership was not met. Sources said the session would be the stormiest in recent times. State BJP president Ramdas Agrawal asserted since the party had the support of 108 legislators in the house of 200, with one seat vacant, there was no threat to the government. Meanwhile Congress, the main opposition party, decided not to introduce a no-confidence motion against the government during the session, but to support any such move if initiated by the BJP rebels.
The Economic Times
FINAL DRAFT OF NEW TAKEOVER CODE SUBMITTED

The final draft of the new takeover guidelines has been submitted to the stock market regulator by the draft committee. Equality of treatment to all shareholders, protection of shareholder interests and fair and truthful disclosure of all material information by acquirers form part of the guiding principles of the draft. Stringent monetary penalties and disqualification of directors of the acquirer who violate the regulations were recommended.
STEEL MAJOR'S STAKE IN SUBSIDIARY TO COME DOWN TO 49 PCT

The stake of Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) in its ailing subsidiary, Indian Iron and Steel Company (IISCO), is slated to fall to 49 percent once the final revival plan is approved by the government. Minister for Steel and Mines B.P. Baishya said Russian giant Tyazpromexport (TPE) would pick up a 39 percent stake in IISCO. The West Bengal government and the workers' union would pick up six percent each, leaving SAIL with 49 percent in the company, Baishya said.
Financial Express
NEW FOREIGN INSTITUTIONAL INVESTORS ENTER MARKET

As many as 10 new foreign institutional investors have entered the domestic market since January 1, 1997. During the first 15 days of this month, an estimated $15 million have been invested. Almost all of these new funds, according to dealers, are U.S. and Europe-based, and none are from South East Asia as in the past. Included in the list are German Deutsche Bank's' DB Fund, U.S.-based GMO Trust, Templeton's World Growth Fund, Emerging Markets State Fund, Lexington, AP Trust of the United Kingdom and a couple of Japanese funds such as Nomura.
COUNTER-GUARANTEE FOR POWER PROJECTS BY FEBRUARY

The Power Minister said the government will clear counter-guarantees for all remaining fast track private power projects by February. Thereafter, there would be no more guarantee and the projects would be a guarantee in themselves, he added. Admitting that initiatives to involve the private sector in creating power capacity failed due to inexperience, he expressed the hope that half of the capacity addition during the ninth plan would be from the private sector.
$120 MLN APEX BANK BID TO CHECK MONOPOLY

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has invited tenders from seven international companies for the supply of 400 million pieces of currency notes in denominations of 500 and 100 rupees. The order is worth $120 million. The RBI has been compelled to look for an international supplier as capacities of the note presses in the country are currently inadequate to print the notes required. As many as 17 companies have procured tender documents from RBI while seven companies, including the British company Thomas De La Rue Plc, have made detailed presentations on what they can offer.
INFLATION MOVES UP TO 7.75 PCT

Maintaining its upward trend, the annual rate of inflation rose marginally to 7.75 percent for the week ended January 4, 1997. The annual inflation (provisional over final) went up by 0.10 percentage point compared to 7.65 percent during the previous week. The wholesale prices index for all commodities also registered a 0.10 percent increase to 319.8 points from 319.5 during the week. The annual inflation in the first week of 1996 was 5.2 percent.
Business Standard
PROPRIETARY FOREIGN FUNDS TO BE ALLOWED

The entry of proprietary foreign institutional investor (FII) funds into the markets is being planned by the stock market regulator SEBI. The move will enable FIIs to deploy their own funds in the Indian market. Until now, FIIs were allowed to invest funds only on behalf of their clients. The move is expected to spark a massive inflow of FII funds into India, regulatory officials said. The Reserve bank has cleared the proposal and SEBI will now approach the government to endorse it. There is also a proposal to allow proprietary FII funds to invest in the debt market where the government recently permitted FIIs to invest their client's funds.
GDP GROWTH TARGET UNDER CLOUD

The 6.6 percent growth target of gross domestic product (GDP) in the current fiscal has come under a cloud, following reports that agricultural output may be much lower than anticipated. Agriculture was expected to make up for the loss of steam in the industrial sector and mitigate any shortfall in the overall growth targets. But with the delayed onset of winter rains, some doubts have been expressed on the output in the current year. The National Council for Applied Economic Research in its revised estimates for the year has fixed GDP growth at 5.9 percent, lower than the projection of 6.3 per cent made in September. They have, however, retained the agricultural growth rate at 4.1 percent but have scaled down industrial growth targets to 9.3 percent, initially pegged at 10.2 percent.
UPLINK MOOTED FOR PRIVATE FIRMS

The Information and Broadcasting Ministry recommended to the cabinet that all private broadcasters should be allowed to uplink from India subject to a 30 percent cap on foreign equity in the broadcasting company. The ministry also favoured permitting private radio and television stations with the restriction on the number of such stations a single company could set up. At present only state-owned Doordarshan is allowed to uplink from India. Media analysts said if uplinking was allowed from India subject to a cap on foreign equity, companies like TV India and ATL would have to restructure themselves and foreign holding brought down to the prescribed limit.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS INSIST ON CONSOLIDATED STATEMENT

As part of their recommendations on corporate governance, financial institutions (FIs) have recommended consolidated financial statements for group companies with cross holdings above a cutoff point. They also recommended compulsory publication of financial results on a quarterly basis, as is the practice abroad. The recommendations have been sent to the finance ministry for its approval, following which the guidelines would be announced by the FIs.
The Observer
FOREIGN INVESTMENT BOARD'S NOD MUST FOR TAKEOVERS

The new takeover code has made it mandatory for foreign companies to get the Foreign Investment Promotion Board's (FIPB) approval for acquiring Indian companies. The code also stipulated a specific time period for FIPB to respond to the applications. The code said if FIPB failed to respond within specific time period, these would be deemed automatically approved. Officials sources said the clause had put FIPB in a quandary. Officials argued that the concept of the takeover applications coming through the FIPB route was new and it needed expertise to handle such cases. If time-bound clearances of applications were forced upon FIPB, it might have difficulties in discerning the right applications from the wrong ones, they added.
Business Line
COAL INDIA'S SUBSIDIARIES TO GET AUTONOMY

Coal India Ltd (CIL) has decided to give more functional autonomy to its eight subsidiaries. The objective behind the move is to make each subsidiary an independent profit centre. Under the new guidelines, the subsidiaries would be responsible for their own ways and of the subsidiaries. The holding company's direct obligation to organise funds for them would, therefore, diminish. It would be the responsibility of the subsidiaries to arrange working capital as well as funds for modernisation and expansion of the existing mines and development of new mines.
